findings.note: countingStore.Lock reads and writes the shared firstLock field without holding c.mu, while Append and EventsWithLines on the same struct do take the mutex. The mutex's presence implies these fakes are exercised from more than one goroutine (fork paths lock a second run), so the failLockRun="child" bookkeeping is an unsynchronized read/write that -race could flag. Test-only, no production impact.

evidence.note: Lock() mutates c.firstLock and compares against it with no c.mu guard, unlike Append/EventsWithLines above and below it

findings.note: failure() caps field values with run.CapText(v, run.MaxShort) only on the errs.Error branch; the StoreError and FoldError branches write fe.Reason/fe.Type into fields uncapped, so an unusually long fold reason lands in the envelope at full length (detail itself is still capped by MaxDetail). Cosmetic inconsistency in output bounding, not a correctness or safety defect.
